entries.name: QuoteWerks
entries.definition: Software for creating sales quotes, proposals and orders that links to accounting, CRM and distributor product data.

entries.name: Rack elevation drawings
entries.definition: Preparing or reading drawings that show the front view of an equipment rack and where each device sits in it.

entries.name: Radare2
entries.definition: An open-source framework of command-line tools for disassembling, debugging and analysing binary files.

entries.name: Rail safety
entries.definition: Practices, rules and equipment used to prevent accidents and injuries on railways.

entries.name: Railway signalling
entries.definition: The systems and rules that control train movements and keep trains apart, such as signals, track circuits and interlockings.

entries.name: Rally Software
entries.definition: An agile project-management and portfolio-planning tool, made by Rally Software and later owned by CA Technologies and then Broadcom.

entries.name: Rancher
entries.definition: An open-source platform for deploying and managing many Kubernetes clusters, developed by Rancher Labs and later SUSE.

entries.name: Random forest
entries.definition: A machine-learning method that builds many decision trees on random samples of the data and combines their outputs for classification or regression.

entries.name: Random testing
entries.definition: Testing software by giving it randomly generated inputs and checking that it behaves correctly.

entries.name: Random variable
entries.definition: A quantity whose value depends on the outcome of a random process and is described by a probability distribution.

entries.name: Randomization
entries.definition: Using chance to assign subjects to groups, order items or pick samples so that no systematic bias creeps in.

entries.name: Rankine cycle
entries.definition: A thermodynamic cycle, used in steam power plants, in which water is boiled, expanded through a turbine, condensed and pumped back to the boiler.

entries.name: RavenDB
entries.definition: A NoSQL document database that stores JSON documents and supports ACID transactions.

entries.name: Ray tracing
entries.definition: A rendering technique that makes images by following the paths of light rays through a scene and calculating how they bounce off and pass through surfaces.

entries.name: React
entries.definition: A user-interface library; not synonymous with React Native.

entries.name: ReactiveX
entries.definition: A family of libraries, such as RxJava and RxJS, for writing asynchronous and event-driven programs by composing streams of events called observables.

entries.name: Reading gauges
entries.definition: Reading analog or digital gauges to check pressure, temperature, levels or flow on equipment.

entries.name: Reading technical drawings
entries.definition: Reading technical drawings such as blueprints and schematics to understand the shapes, dimensions and instructions they show.

entries.name: Reading to children
entries.definition: Reading books and stories aloud to children, for example to build their listening, language and interest in reading.

entries.name: ReadyAPI
entries.definition: A SmartBear suite of tools for testing and monitoring APIs, covering functional, security and load testing.

entries.name: Real estate
entries.definition: Land and the buildings on it, and the field of buying, selling, leasing, valuing and managing them.

entries.name: Real estate contracts
entries.definition: The agreements, such as purchase, sale and lease contracts, used to transfer or let property, and the rules on how they are written and enforced.

entries.name: Real estate market analysis
entries.definition: Studying prices, supply, demand and trends in a property market to judge the value of properties and the prospects of an area.

entries.name: Real estate owned
entries.definition: Property that a lender owns after it fails to sell at a foreclosure auction, and the work of managing and reselling it.

entries.name: Real-time payments
entries.definition: Payment systems that clear and settle transfers between bank accounts within seconds, at any hour, such as the RTP network and FedNow.

entries.name: Receptive and expressive language
entries.definition: The two sides of language ability studied in speech-language pathology: understanding what others say or write, and putting thoughts into words.

entries.name: Recruitment consulting
entries.definition: Advising employers on hiring and finding, screening and placing candidates for them.

entries.name: Red teaming
entries.definition: Playing the part of an adversary to test how well an organisation, system or AI model withstands attack or misuse.

entries.name: REDCap
entries.definition: A web application, developed at Vanderbilt University, for building and managing online surveys and research databases.

entries.name: Reduction (complexity)
entries.definition: A way of converting one problem into another so that a solution to the second gives a solution to the first, used in complexity theory to compare how hard problems are.

entries.name: Reference range
entries.definition: The range of values for a laboratory test that is expected in healthy people, used to judge whether a result is normal.

entries.name: Refrigerated transport
entries.definition: Moving perishable or temperature-sensitive goods in vehicles or containers that keep them cold.

entries.name: Refrigeration
entries.definition: The technology and practice of removing heat to keep a space or product colder than its surroundings, as in cold rooms, freezers and chillers.

entries.name: Refrigeration compressors
entries.definition: The machines that compress refrigerant gas in a refrigeration system so that it can circulate and carry heat away.

entries.name: Refugee issues
entries.definition: Understanding the legal, social and humanitarian circumstances of people forced to flee their countries, and the services that support them.

entries.name: Registered Education Savings Plan
entries.definition: A Canadian government-registered savings account, with grants, for a child's education after high school, and the planning of contributions to it.

entries.name: Regulation SHO
entries.definition: A U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission regulation governing short sales of securities, including locate and close-out requirements.

entries.name: Regulatory CMC
entries.definition: Preparing and managing the chemistry, manufacturing and controls information that regulators require in applications for drugs and biological products.

entries.name: Rehabilitation
entries.definition: Treatment and training that help a person recover or regain abilities and independence lost through injury, illness, disability or addiction.

entries.name: Reinforced masonry
entries.definition: Masonry construction in which steel bars or mesh are embedded in mortar or grout so that walls resist tension, bending and earthquake loads.
